evidence.note: Claim: a stale reading over the line must still pause and a missing one must not; mechanism: decide() counts fraction>=pause_at only where a figure exists; falsifier: test_a_stale_figure_over_the_line_still_pauses / test_an_unmeasured_window_has_no_fraction_and_does_not_pause fail. tests/test_quota_eval.py 18 pass
D-quotas-governor (pure services module, no event/CLI), r-bounded-everything (pause_at and recheck_s validated), unknown/unlimited never pause
ddflow/services/quota_eval.py evaluate/decide/resume; tests/test_quota_eval.py (18) fail before (no module), pass; guards/counters/import contracts pass

chunk_findings.detail: `_one` computes `r.value / w.limit` for every `B.OK` reading without ensuring `w.limit` is nonzero. Given a limited profile containing a window whose limit is `0.0` and a meter reading with `status=B.OK` and `value=0.0`, `evaluate` raises `ZeroDivisionError` instead of returning a `WindowEval`. A zero allowance is not the same as the unlimited profile state, so the module either needs to define the fraction/pause behavior for zero limits or reject such windows before division.
chunk_findings.title: quota_eval.py:_one

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that when the only known `resets_at` is already in the past, `decide` returns `resume_at == NOW` even though the window is still over the pause line. With `profile(W5H)`, a 95% reading whose reset was `2026-11-12T11:00:00+00:00`, `now=2026-11-12T12:00:00Z`, `pause_at=0.9`, and `recheck_interval=300`, the asserted result is a pause whose resume time is the current instant. A caller that pauses until `resume_at` and then re-evaluates at the same `now` will immediately get the same pause again, producing a zero-delay loop. This contradicts both the stated contract that `resume_at` is the next reset and the adjacent test for an unknown reset, which correctly falls back to `NOW + recheck_interval`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_quota_eval.py:93

chunk_findings.detail: In `_one`, `resets = (r.resets_at if r else "") or _fixed_reset(w, now)` lets a non-empty `resets_at` from a stale reading suppress the fixed-window calculation. For a fixed window with anchor `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` and period 3600 seconds, evaluated at `1970-01-01T02:00:00Z`, a stale OK reading whose `resets_at` is from the previous period (`1970-01-01T01:00:00Z`) and whose value is at the limit makes `_one` return that past reset. `decide` then sees a reset not ahead and returns `now + recheck_s` instead of the next fixed reset (`1970-01-01T03:00:00Z`), so the resume/recheck time is wrong and can cause repeated immediate rechecks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/quota_eval.py:67

chunk_findings.detail: `recheck_s <= 0` does not reject `float("nan")`. Given `decide(evals, 1.0, now, float("nan"))` where any over-window has no future reset, validation passes because `nan <= 0` is false, then `_resume_at` returns `now + float("nan")`, producing `Decision.resume_at = nan` even though the contract says resume_at is epoch seconds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/quota_eval.py:108

chunk_findings.detail: `resume((), pause_at)` returns `True` because `all([])` is vacuously true. This makes a paused subject resume whenever the current evaluation list is empty, even if that emptiness comes from a missing/unknown profile or a failed evaluation rather than from the subject actually becoming unlimited. For example, if a subject was paused because its 5-hour window exceeded the pause threshold, and later the quota profile is temporarily unavailable so the caller passes `()` to `resume`, the function returns `True` and the subject resumes despite there being no fresh quota figure below the line—contradicting the stated rule that a missing figure is not evidence that quota came back.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/quota_eval.py:resume

chunk_findings.detail: When no window has a fraction, `decide` always explains a run as "nothing limits or measures this subject". That is false for a limited profile that simply was not read. `test_the_run_reason_does_not_claim_a_measurement_that_never_happened` builds exactly that input — `evaluate(profile(W5H), [], NOW)` — and only checks that `"nothing"` appears in the reason, so the new string is accepted even though W5H is a limit and the only true fact is that no measurement exists. A caller that treats that reason as "this subject is unlimited" will skip a real quota.

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added empty-evaluation branch returns the reason `"no window limits this subject"` whenever `evals` is empty. The same change’s `resume` docstring explicitly says an empty evaluation list can mean “a profile that was lost or failed to read” as well as a profile that stopped limiting, so `()` is not proof that no window limits the subject. chunk_findings.detail: The new guard treats every profile state other than `"limited"` as an immediate resume, so `profile.state == "unknown"` returns `True`. “Unknown” is not the same as a known unlimited profile: it is the state used for a profile that cannot be read or whose limits are not known (the new test itself uses `quota.Profile("a", unknown=True)`). Given a subject that was paused under a limited profile, if the next evaluation yields an unknown profile while the subject may still be over quota, `resume` returns `True` and the caller resumes without evidence that the quota came back. The intent only says unlimited profiles never pause; it does not authorize resuming on unknown, and the previous docstring warned that a lost/failed profile read is not evidence of an all-clear.

chunk_findings.detail: The new short-circuit `if profile.state != "limited": return True` treats an unknown profile as an all-clear. For example, if a subject was paused under a limited profile and the profile lookup later fails, returning `quota.Profile("a", unknown=True)` with no fresh evaluations, `Q.resume(profile, (), 0.9)` returns `True` even though there is no evidence that the quota came back. The added test codifies this fail-open path. This conflicts with the module’s stated invariant that missing/stale figures and an empty evaluation list are not evidence to resume; only an explicitly unlimited profile is described by the intent as never limiting.
